chain.label: Gusty northwesterly crosswind at MEM
chain.trigger: sustained winds 15 to 20 minutes before and after the accident were consistently from the northwest at 17 to 23 knots...gusts to 26/28 knots

chain.label: Inadequate emergency door/slide trainer and hands-on training
chain.trigger: there was no girt bar flap assembly (and, thus, no manual inflation or disengage handles) installed on FedEx's MD-11/-10 emergency exit door/slide trainer...training program did not require crewmembers to simulate pulling a manual inflation handle

chain.label: First officer neutralized crosswind correction inputs before touchdown
chain.trigger: these normal crosswind landing control inputs were only momentary...the aileron and rudder control inputs were neutralized and remained neutral until the airplane touched down

caused_by.evidence: the winds at the time of the accident would have required a pilot's constant attention, significant flight control inputs...and continuous modulation of those inputs

chain.label: First officer failed to flare and arrest descent rate before touchdown
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's FDR data showed that the first officer did not increase the airplane's pitch attitude to arrest the airplane's rate of descent

chain.label: Captain failed to monitor and correct first officer's performance
chain.trigger: the captain, who was conducting a line check of the first officer, did not adequately monitor the first officer's performance during the final stages of the approach and landing...and failed to take or initiate corrective action to prevent the accident

chain.label: Excessive vertical and lateral loads on right main landing gear at touchdown
chain.trigger: the excessive vertical and lateral forces on the right main landing gear during the landing exceeded those that the gear was designed to withstand

caused_by.evidence: peak lateral loads coincided with the excessive vertical loads
the first officer did not increase the airplane's pitch attitude to arrest the airplane's rate of descent
the captain...failed to take or initiate corrective action to prevent the accident

chain.label: Right main landing gear outer cylinder fractured and gear collapsed
chain.trigger: the right main landing gear collapsed during the landing roll, and the outer cylinder fractured into six pieces

caused_by.evidence: resulted in the fracture of the outer cylinder and the collapse of the right main landing gear

chain.label: Airplane veered off runway and postcrash fire developed
chain.trigger: the airplane veered off the right side of the runway. After the gear collapsed, a fire developed on the right side of the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the right main landing gear collapsed after touchdown on runway 36R, and the airplane veered off the right side of the runway

chain.label: Nonrevenue pilot mistakenly pulled slide disengage handle with inflation handle
chain.trigger: the nonrevenue FedEx pilot...mistakenly pulled both the manual inflation and slide/raft disengage handles because he was not sufficiently familiar with their location and operation

caused_by.evidence: FedEx's door trainer configuration eliminated an opportunity for FedEx crewmembers to become familiar with the location and appearance of these handles

chain.label: L1 evacuation slide/raft separated from the airplane
chain.trigger: the slide/raft inflated, separated from the doorsill, and disappeared under the airplane

caused_by.evidence: thus separating the slide/raft from the L1 doorsill

chain.label: Crewmembers delayed evacuation to retrieve personal bags
chain.trigger: it is evident that the delays were the result of the offloading of crewmembers' personal bags...and not because they were waiting for other crewmembers to exit

chain.label: Minor injuries sustained during cockpit-window evacuation
chain.trigger: the first officer sustained friction burns to both hands while sliding down the evacuation tape, and...the cockpit jumpseat occupant sustained minor injuries when he landed on his right shoulder after he let go of the evacuation tape

caused_by.evidence: fire on the right side of the airplane
the airplane occupants exited through the cockpit window exits
the elapsed time between successive crewmembers exiting the airplane was as much as 63 seconds
